stem: In the figure, line \(CD\) is parallel to line \(EF\). Point \(A\) lies on line \(CD\), and point \(B\) lies on line \(EF\). What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: Draw a line through \(P\) parallel to the two given lines. It splits angle \(APB\) into two parts.
The upper part is an alternate interior angle with the \(35^{\circ}\) angle, and the lower part is an alternate interior angle with the \(48^{\circ}\) angle.
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['C'][1]==P['D'][1] and P['E'][1]==P['F'][1]
assert abs(ang('D','A','P')-35)<0.1 and abs(ang('F','B','P')-48)<0.1
ans=35+48
assert abs(ang('A','P','B')-ans)<0.1
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==83
